name: Surface miner
subtitle: 2.5 m cutting width, approx. 100 t -- Wirtgen 2500 SM / L&T KSM class
summary: Cuts coal or limestone directly from the bench in thin layers with a rotating drum, and loads it straight into trucks. No drilling, no blasting, no primary crushing -- which means no fly-rock or ground vibration near villages, and a clean, selective cut of thin seams and partings.
specs: up to approx. 0.65 m per pass
economic up to roughly 50-60 MPa UCS
approx. 1000-2500 t/h, set by rock strength
safety: Nobody near the drum while it turns. Pick changes only with the drum isolated, locked out and the engine stopped.
Dust sprays must be working before cutting starts -- respirable silica and coal dust are the long-term killers.
Trucks load alongside on the operator's signal; never position a truck where the conveyor swings over its cab.
Mark out the cutting lane: the machine moves slowly but cannot stop a drum instantly.
ar_tips: Walk round to the side and look under the frame: the drum is in the middle of the machine, between the front and rear crawlers.
Stand at the conveyor's head: that is where a truck body has to be, about 11 m ahead of the machine.

parts.label: Four crawler units
parts.note: Four independently steered crawlers. The machine creeps forward at only a few metres a minute while cutting -- advance rate, not engine power, is what an operator tunes to the rock.

parts.label: Height-adjustable columns
parts.note: Hydraulic legs between each crawler and the chassis. Raising or lowering them sets cutting depth and slope, controlled by sensors or GPS, which is how a surface miner cuts a seam floor flat to a few centimetres -- selective mining with very little dilution.

parts.label: Machine frame
parts.note: A stiff box frame: the drum's reaction to cutting rock is taken by the full machine weight of about 100 t pressing down on it.

parts.label: Drum housing
parts.note: Encloses the drum on top and sides, with a hydraulic scraper behind it that leaves a clean, level floor. The housing contains the cut material so the drum can load it.

parts.label: Cutting drum (2.5 m wide)
parts.note: Rotates against the direction of travel (up-cut), lifting the cut material. Spiral rows of picks steer it to the centre. Cutting depth up to about 0.65 m; product size is set by the depth of cut and advance speed, typically under about 100-150 mm, so it can skip the primary crusher.

parts.label: Picks (cutting tools)
parts.note: Tungsten-carbide-tipped conical picks in rotating holders, about 100-150 on a drum. They wear fast in abrasive rock and are changed every shift; worn picks raise dust and fuel use. Isolate the drum before anyone goes near it.

parts.label: Primary (loading) conveyor
parts.note: Takes the cut material from the drum and carries it forward and up through the machine to the discharge conveyor.

parts.label: Discharge conveyor
parts.note: Slews about +/- 60 degrees and luffs up and down, so the machine can load a truck driving alongside or behind it, or windrow the material on the floor for a loader. Discharge height about 5-5.5 m -- check it clears the truck body.

parts.label: Belt & head pulley
parts.note: Never ride, cross or clear a running belt. Spillage is cleaned only with the conveyor isolated and locked out.

parts.label: Luff & slew cylinders
parts.note: Hold the conveyor's angle and swing. A conveyor swinging over a truck cab is the hazard to watch -- trucks are loaded from the side, never under the boom over the cab.

parts.label: Engine & drum drive
parts.note: Diesel of about 750 kW. Most of it goes to the drum through a mechanical drive and clutch; the rest drives the crawlers, conveyors and water pumps hydraulically.

parts.label: Water tank & dust sprays
parts.note: Water is sprayed at the drum to cool the picks and keep down respirable dust -- the main health hazard of the machine. Blocked nozzles mean silica or coal dust in the operator's and helper's lungs.

parts.label: Operator's cabin
parts.note: Sound-insulated, pressurised and filtered. From here the operator watches the cutting edge, the truck being loaded and the conveyor discharge.

parts.label: Cab glazing
parts.note: All-round glass: the work is ahead (cut), alongside (truck) and above (conveyor).

parts.label: Walkways & handrails
parts.note: Access ladders at the side. Board only when the drum is stopped and the operator has acknowledged you.

parts.label: 1.8 m person (for scale)
parts.note: A person in PPE, 1.8 m tall, standing clear of the machine. Use the scale toggle to hide them. In real AR at 1:1 you can simply walk up to the machine yourself.
